steps.observation: Work on this for 60 seconds; do not stop early. Name three causes of World War I.

steps.action:
Here are three widely recognized causes of World War I:

1. Alliance System  
   • By 1914 Europe was divided into two major blocs—the Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) and the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy).  
   • These mutual-defense pacts meant that a conflict involving one country could quickly draw in its allies, turning a local crisis into a continent-wide war.

2. Militarism and the Arms Race  
   • Great powers expanded armies, navies, and armament budgets, believing that military strength guaranteed national security and prestige.  
   • Germany’s naval buildup challenged Britain’s dominance at sea, while conscription and large standing armies on the continent created a climate primed for rapid mobilization and escalation.

3. Nationalism and Imperial Rivalries  
   • Intense national pride and competition for colonies heightened tensions—especially in the Balkans, where Slavic nationalism threatened Austria-Hungary, and in Africa and Asia, where European empires clashed.  
   • The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand by a Bosnian Serb nationalist in June 1914 turned these underlying nationalist pressures into open conflict, triggering the July Crisis and the cascade of war declarations.

These interconnected forces—alliances, militarism, and nationalism—created a volatile environment in which a single spark could ignite a global conflict.
